Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create a NEW module. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no live Gmail calls in tests: the email client is INJECTED and mocked.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 7 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/guest_assets.py
  tests/test_guest_assets_wiring.py
  tests/test_guest_email_context.py

THE FAILURE, real and embarrassing. The repo already has server/pipeline/guest_email_context.py with gather_guest_email_context() and download_headshot(). Run against a real guest today it immediately returned:
  headshots: [{"filename": "prof headshot minimized.webp", "mime_type": "image/webp",
               "size_bytes": 645648, "message_id": "...", "attachment_id": "..."}]
  links: {"linkedin": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/fredhcho/",
          "website": "https://www.fredhcho.com/",
          "other": ["https://podcasts.apple.com/ca/podcast/20-happy-careers-..."]}
The guest sent his headshot and his links weeks ago. NOTHING IN THE PIPELINE EVER CALLED THAT MODULE. The episode published with a thumbnail that does not use the guest's photo, and show notes carrying only the LinkedIn URL from the CRM record while his website and his own podcast were sitting unread in the inbox. The capability existed and was never wired. That is the defect: not a missing feature, an unused one.

BUILD server/pipeline/guest_assets.py — the wiring layer that makes the existing capability actually run:

  collect_guest_assets(client, guest_email, dest_dir, *, existing_links=None) -> dict
      Calls gather_guest_email_context, then download_headshot for the BEST headshot
      candidate, and returns:
        {"headshot_path": str|None, "headshot_source": {...}|None,
         "links": {...merged...}, "bio_candidates": [...],
         "skipped": [{"what","reason"}]}
      BEST candidate selection, deterministic and documented: prefer an attachment whose
      filename suggests a headshot or portrait, then the largest image under the size cap,
      then the most recent. Ties break on filename so two runs never disagree.
      LINK MERGING: links found in the guest's own email WIN over `existing_links` for the
      same key, because the guest is authoritative about their own URLs, but a key present
      only in existing_links is preserved. Never drop a link, never invent one.
      Any failure to download is recorded in "skipped" with a reason and returns
      headshot_path None. It must NEVER raise: a missing headshot degrades the episode, it
      does not stop it.

  thumbnail_source(guest_assets, *, fallback) -> (str, str)
      Returns (path, reason). The guest's emailed headshot wins when present; otherwise the
      supplied fallback with a reason naming why the headshot was not used. The reason
      string is what a human reads when asking "why isn't the guest's face on this".

  assets_report(guest_assets) -> str
      A short human-readable summary: which headshot was used and from which message, which
      links were found and from where, and anything skipped. This is what makes an unused
      capability visible next time: if the report says "no headshot found" and the guest
      did send one, that is now a legible bug rather than silence.

  Never log or return a raw message body. Never write outside dest_dir.

TESTS (tests/test_guest_assets_wiring.py, fake client; at least 7):
 (1) THE REAL CASE: a client whose messages include an image/webp attachment named
     "prof headshot minimized.webp" yields a headshot_path, and thumbnail_source prefers it
     over the fallback;
 (2) NEGATIVE: with NO image attachment, thumbnail_source returns the fallback AND a reason
     that names the absence — silence is not acceptable;
 (3) link merging: a website found in the guest's email overrides an empty/absent value in
     existing_links, and an existing key not present in the email is preserved;
 (4) NEGATIVE: a download that raises is recorded in "skipped" and collect_guest_assets
     returns normally with headshot_path None — a bad attachment never breaks an episode;
 (5) best-candidate selection is deterministic across two identical runs;
 (6) NEGATIVE: no raw message body appears anywhere in the returned structure (assert a
     distinctive body string is absent);
 (7) assets_report names the chosen headshot and the links found;
 (8) NEGATIVE: a non-image attachment (application/pdf) is never chosen as a headshot.
Keep tests/test_guest_email_context.py green.
